bug_description.normalized: In sudoers editor resolution, a string allocated for the candidate editor name is registered in the sudoers garbage-collector list, then freed on an ENOENT or OOM failure path without removing its GC entry. Later sudoers_gc_run() walks the stale GC entry and frees the same pointer again, producing a heap double free.

source.description: sudoers_policy_open() consumes the attacker-controlled `sudoedit=on` setting and parse_bool() sets MODE_EDIT in `flags`, creating the edit-mode state that drives the vulnerable editor-resolution path.

sink.description: sudoers_gc_run() frees a stale GC_PTR entry whose payload is the same editor string already freed earlier in resolve_editor().

root_cause.description: On the `find_path(...) != FOUND` failure path, resolve_editor() frees `editor` but does not call sudoers_gc_remove(GC_PTR, editor), leaving a dangling GC entry that is later freed again.

parser_admitted.description: The sample-specific `sudoedit=on` line is accepted by the policy option parser and converted into MODE_EDIT state.

tainted_value_origin.description: The fuzz input setting `sudoedit=on` is parsed into the policy mode flags, setting MODE_EDIT for later control flow.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzzed settings include `sudoedit=on`, so the policy parser enables MODE_EDIT for subsequent policy operations.
Edit mode causes sudoers_policy_main() to call find_editor() to resolve an editor command.
resolve_editor() allocates the editor string, registers it with the sudoers GC list, then on a path-resolution failure frees it without unregistering it.
At fuzz-target teardown, sudoers_gc_run() walks the stale GC entry and frees the already-freed editor pointer a second time.

fine_trace.note: The fuzz input line `sudoedit=on` is consumed by parse_bool(), which sets MODE_EDIT in the policy flags used by later sudoers logic.
Because MODE_EDIT is set, sudoers_policy_main() takes the sudoedit path and calls find_editor() instead of keeping the existing command vector.
resolve_editor() copies the chosen editor token with copy_arg(); copy_arg() allocates the string and immediately registers that allocation in the sudoers GC list via sudoers_gc_add(GC_PTR, copy).

When find_path(editor, ...) does not return FOUND, resolve_editor() frees the GC-tracked `editor` string on the ENOENT path and returns NULL, but vulnerable code does not remove that GC_PTR entry first.

At the end of LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(), sudoers_gc_run() starts draining the global GC list; the stale entry for the freed `editor` pointer is still present because no sudoers_gc_remove() ran on the failure path.
For a GC_PTR entry, sudoers_gc_run() frees the stored pointer. When that entry still references the earlier-freed `editor` allocation, this second free triggers the ASAN heap-double-free.

poc.trigger: The witnessed fuzz_policy input includes `sudoedit=on`, which makes sudoers take the MODE_EDIT path and attempt editor resolution; on the staged failing run, unresolved editor lookup frees a GC-tracked editor string in resolve_editor(), and the later sudoers_gc_run() call frees the stale entry again.

format.contract: A witnessed crashing input is a valid fuzz_policy text file accepted by sudoers_policy_open() that includes `sudoedit=on` and reaches the same unresolved-editor failure path in the staged environment. The runtime evidence here shows that this path leaves a GC-tracked editor allocation freed in resolve_editor() and freed again by sudoers_gc_run(); no broader input class is claimed.
